title: Local coordinates and reference-point continuum coupling
summary: Maps explicit local components to global finite-element loads and applies force/moment or known rigid motion through a named continuum reference point.

science.statement: A right-handed orthonormal basis makes component conventions explicit; remote resultants and known rigid motions are then transferred to a continuum boundary without a singular solid-node force.

equations.label: local-to-global vector
equations.description: Rows of Q are local basis vectors expressed in global components.

equations.label: rigid boundary motion
equations.description: The prescribed displacement is evaluated on every constrained boundary dof.

equations.label: remote resultant
equations.expression: integral_Gamma t dGamma = F_RP; integral_Gamma (x-x_RP) x t dGamma = M_RP
equations.description: The distributing traction preserves force and moment about the named point.

inputs.name: coordinate system and reference point
inputs.type: orthonormal basis, origin, and finite point coordinates
inputs.description: Local axes must be right handed and match the model dimension.

outputs.name: continuum load or strong rigid-motion constraint
outputs.type: weak boundary load or Dirichlet asset
outputs.description: Both assets are consumed by ordinary model steps and retain engineering summaries.

assumptions: The selected surface has sufficient geometric extent to transmit a requested moment.
remote_displacement specifies known rigid motion rather than solving for an independent reference-point degree of freedom.
conventions: Coordinate-system axes are stored by row in global components.
Two-dimensional rotation and moment are scalar out-of-plane quantities.
Constant remote displacement follows the normalized nonlinear load path.
applicability: Fixture coordinates, remote loading, driven grips, and continuum-solid coupling surfaces.
limitations: An unknown kinematic reference-point degree of freedom and general MPC coupling are not implemented by this contract.
Local component constraints on an arbitrary oblique direction require a dedicated MPC rather than a component Dirichlet approximation.

usage.minimal_example: local = coordinates.cartesian(x=(0,1), y=(-1,0)); rp = coordinates.reference_point((2,0.5), name='RP-1'); model.remote_force((3,4), moment=2, reference_point=rp, system=local, on=end)

validation_rules: Reject coordinate, vector, rotation, and target dimension mismatches.
Integrate generated traction and recover transformed force and requested moment.
Verify remote motion follows deterministic load-factor scaling.
